requirements.requirement: The system must map lead_sponsor.agency_class = 'NIH' to a predefined high credibility score within the 0-1 range.
The system must map lead_sponsor.agency_class = 'Industry' to a predefined credibility score lower than NIH but within the 0-1 range.
The system must map lead_sponsor.agency_class = 'Other' to a predefined credibility score lower than Industry.
The system must infer 'Academic' sponsor type when agency_class is not explicitly provided but the sponsor name contains known academic indicators (e.g., 'University', 'College').
The system must assign all computed credibility scores as normalized float values between 0 and 1 inclusive.
The system must produce deterministic outputs such that identical sponsor inputs always yield the same credibility score.
The system must adjust the base credibility score upward when one or more collaborators have higher credibility classifications than the lead sponsor.
The system must not allow collaborator influence to increase the final credibility score beyond the maximum bound of 1.0.
The system must handle multiple collaborators by applying a deterministic aggregation rule (e.g., max or weighted average) to influence the final score.
The system must return a default fallback credibility score when lead_sponsor data is missing.
The system must assign a lowest-tier credibility score when agency_class is present but not recognized in the mapping.
The system must handle null or empty collaborator lists without throwing errors and proceed with lead sponsor-only scoring.
The system must expose intermediate classification (e.g., resolved sponsor_type) used in scoring for downstream explanation generation.
The system must ensure that collaborator influence rules do not reduce the base credibility score derived from the lead sponsor.
